q: “The satisfaction of wants is known as consumption”, explain this statement?
a: Answers: Consumption: We use things to satisfy our wants; this action is known as "Consumption" in Economics, e.g. we eat food to satisfy our hunger and take water when we feel thirst. In other words, consumption means the use of goods and services which satisfy our wants. Consumption is closely related to Income because a man will spend on consumption as much as he earns. When income is less, consumption will also be less. By means of the consumption of goods and services, we satisfy our wants. The utility of a certain good must be immediately e.g. food, water, tea, coffee newspaper, etc. while many goods possess long-lasting utility e.g. books, pens, cars, tables, chairs, dresses, motorcycles, and houses, etc. Write short notes on; Income By "Income" we mean the payment received by a man against his services e.g. A laborer works physically, whole the day and gets the remuneration (payment) in the evening. A clerk works in an office and gets a salary at the end of the month. A cobbler makes shoes and receives wages at the end of every week. These incomes are received by them after a pre-decided period i.e. daily, weekly, monthly, or annually. e.g. a man works in an office for Rs.2000 per month. It means his monthly income is Rs.2000. Personal Income It is the individual income of a person. E.g. A man owns a business and earns Rs.3000 monthly from it. It will be called his personal income because he earns it from his business. Saving Saving is that part of our income which is told to us after meeting our ordinary expenses. It is the surplus of our income over expenses. E.g. A person's annual income is Rs.25000 and his expenditures are Rs. 20,000. In this case, his annual saving will be Rs.5000).
